question: Which experiences create satisfaction, and what should we protect?

answer.answer_markdown:
**When this bank gets something right, customers say so out loud even while they are complaining - and what they praise is almost always a person who took ownership, not a product or a policy.**

Across the 4,425 complaints in this corpus, 421 calls contain a verified positive moment: a specific thing the bank did that the customer chose to credit in the middle of a grievance. By far the largest kind is helpful staff - 169 calls, 3.8% of the corpus - a named representative who apologised, opened an escalation, or sat with the customer and did the work. The next two are a fair outcome, meaning the bank investigated and paid (124 calls, 2.8%), and fast action, such as spotting and blocking a fraudulent charge or acknowledging a dispute straight away (102 calls, 2.3%). Clear communication - an agent or supervisor plainly confirming what will happen and when - is praised in only 22 calls, 0.5% of the corpus.

Protect four things. First, the escalation path: the empowered representative or supervisor who can break a stuck case is the most praised asset the bank has, so do not automate or offshore that role away. Second, provisional and goodwill credits during disputes - customers forgive the error once the money comes back. Third, proactive fraud blocking, which customers thank the bank for even when they are calling about something else. Fourth, a plain confirmation of the next step and its date; it is the rarest of the four and it lands every time it happens.

Read this honestly. These are positive moments found inside complaints, not a satisfaction survey. Only 2 calls out of 4,425 read as positive overall, only 0.7% end resolved, and none of the 128 active themes is a positive theme - so this says which behaviours customers value when they finally get them, not how satisfied the customer base is. It matters most where the pain is: fraud and unauthorized activity is the biggest contact reason at 1,257 calls (28.4%), and that is exactly where the praised behaviours - investigate, credit, block, escalate - live.

charts.title: Positive moments inside complaints, by category

caveats: These are positive moments found inside complaints, not a satisfaction survey: every call here is a complaint, so the figures show which behaviours customers bother to praise while unhappy, not how satisfied customers are.

Ranking positive topics or themes returns almost nothing - no active theme has positive polarity - which is why the evidence is the verified positive-moment extractions rather than a sentiment ranking.
A positive moment is counted only when a verbatim span in the customer's own words was verified, so these counts are a floor rather than a full measure of good service.
Complaint dates lag the actual contact, and the corpus is public CFPB narratives for one bank written by customers motivated enough to file, so satisfied customers are largely absent by construction.
followups: In the complaints that contain a positive moment, does the case end better (resolved or partially resolved) than in those with none?
Which stage of the fraud and dispute journey earns the praise - first contact, escalation, or the provisional credit - and how long does each take?

confidence.badge: broad pattern · 421 calls · 24 months · 7 products · 45 states

sql.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

SELECT key, COUNT(*) AS n_calls, SUM(CASE WHEN mx > 0 THEN mx ELSE 0 END) AS mass, AVG(mx) AS mean_sentiment FROM (SELECT t.driver_category AS key, t.call_id, MIN(t.sentiment) AS mn, MAX(t.sentiment) AS mx FROM topics t JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY key, t.call_id) GROUP BY key HAVING n_calls >= ? AND mass > 0 ORDER BY mass DESC, key LIMIT ?

SELECT t.driver_category AS key, t.topic_id, t.call_id, t.sentiment, t.driver_category, t.driver FROM topics t JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND t.driver_category IN (?) AND t.sentiment > 0

SELECT t.driver_category AS key, e.evidence_id, e.call_id, e.quote, t.sentiment FROM evidence e JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id = e.topic_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND e.verified = 1 AND t.driver_category IN (?) AND t.sentiment > 0 ORDER BY t.sentiment DESC, c.date DESC, e.evidence_id

SELECT pm.category, COUNT(DISTINCT pm.call_id) AS n_calls FROM positive_moments pm JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = pm.call_id WHERE pm.verified = 1 AND 1=1 GROUP BY pm.category ORDER BY n_calls DESC, pm.category
SELECT pm.category, pm.pm_id, pm.call_id, pm.quote, pm.what FROM positive_moments pm JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = pm.call_id WHERE pm.verified = 1 AND 1=1 ORDER BY c.date DESC

sql.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1
SELECT c.call_id FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM topics t JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = t.call_id WHERE 1=1) AS n_topics, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT tc.theme_id) FROM v_theme_calls tc JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = tc.call_id JOIN themes th ON th.theme_id = tc.theme_id WHERE th.status = 'active' AND 1=1) AS n_themes, (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(1.0 / c.sampling_fraction), 0) FROM calls c WHERE 1=1) AS population_estimate
SELECT c.month, COUNT(*) AS n_calls, ROUND(SUM(1.0 / c.sampling_fraction)) AS population_estimate FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY c.month ORDER BY c.month
SELECT period, population_n FROM period_totals WHERE period_kind = 'month'
SELECT r.reason, COUNT(DISTINCT r.call_id) AS n FROM call_reasons r JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = r.call_id WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY r.reason
SELECT c.month, COUNT(*) AS n FROM calls c WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY c.month ORDER BY c.month
SELECT r.reason, c.month, COUNT(DISTINCT r.call_id) AS n FROM call_reasons r JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = r.call_id WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY r.reason, c.month
SELECT r.reason, r.specific_reason, r.call_id FROM call_reasons r JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = r.call_id WHERE 1=1
SELECT r.reason, r.call_id FROM call_reasons r JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = r.call_id WHERE 1=1 ORDER BY c.date DESC, r.call_id
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM calls c WHERE c.date >= ? AND c.date <= ?
SELECT r.reason, COUNT(DISTINCT r.call_id) AS n FROM call_reasons r JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = r.call_id WHERE c.date >= ? AND c.date <= ? GROUP BY r.reason

SELECT th.theme_id, th.name, th.problem_statement, th.root_cause, th.polarity, th.driver_category, th.n_wordings, th.n_products, COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') AS grouping_quality, th.first_seen_week, es.status AS status_at_as_of, es.emerging_score, COUNT(DISTINCT s.call_id) AS n_calls, SUM(CASE WHEN s.min_sentiment < 0 THEN -s.min_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS neg_mass, SUM(CASE WHEN s.max_sentiment > 0 THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS pos_mass, AVG(CASE WHEN th.polarity = 'positive' THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE s.min_sentiment END) AS mean_sentiment FROM themes th JOIN v_theme_call_sentiment s ON s.theme_id = th.theme_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = s.call_id LEFT JOIN emerging_scores es ON es.entity_type = 'theme' AND es.entity_id = th.theme_id AND es.as_of_week = ? WHERE 1=1 AND th.status = 'active' AND COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') != 'weak' GROUP BY th.theme_id HAVING n_calls >= ? ORDER BY n_calls DESC, th.theme_id LIMIT ?
SELECT tc.theme_id, tc.call_id FROM v_theme_calls tc JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = tc.call_id WHERE 1=1 AND tc.theme_id IN (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ORDER BY c.date DESC, tc.call_id
SELECT e.overall_sentiment AS v, COUNT(*) AS n FROM extractions e JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY v ORDER BY n DESC, v
SELECT e.resolution_status AS v, COUNT(*) AS n FROM extractions e JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY v ORDER BY n DESC, v
SELECT e.customer_ask AS v, COUNT(*) AS n FROM extractions e JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = e.call_id WHERE 1=1 GROUP BY v ORDER BY n DESC, v
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(c.date) AS d0, MAX(c.date) AS d1 FROM calls c WHERE 1=1

SELECT th.theme_id, th.name, th.problem_statement, th.root_cause, th.polarity, th.driver_category, th.n_wordings, th.n_products, COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') AS grouping_quality, th.first_seen_week, es.status AS status_at_as_of, es.emerging_score, COUNT(DISTINCT s.call_id) AS n_calls, SUM(CASE WHEN s.min_sentiment < 0 THEN -s.min_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS neg_mass, SUM(CASE WHEN s.max_sentiment > 0 THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE 0 END) AS pos_mass, AVG(CASE WHEN th.polarity = 'positive' THEN s.max_sentiment ELSE s.min_sentiment END) AS mean_sentiment FROM themes th JOIN v_theme_call_sentiment s ON s.theme_id = th.theme_id JOIN calls c ON c.call_id = s.call_id LEFT JOIN emerging_scores es ON es.entity_type = 'theme' AND es.entity_id = th.theme_id AND es.as_of_week = ? WHERE 1=1 AND th.status = 'active' AND COALESCE(th.grouping_quality, 'ok') != 'weak' AND th.polarity = ? GROUP BY th.theme_id HAVING n_calls >= ? ORDER BY pos_mass DESC, th.theme_id LIMIT ?
